messages:
maya: Quick sync — need to lock the benchmark narrative for launch. Core ask: two clear charts (latency vs $/token and tail-latency tradeoffs), short hero claim + 3 supporting bullets, webinar outline, and inbound routing rules. Attached: proto doc (link) and two sample charts. Can we finalize by EOD tomorrow?

jon: ok, high level — prefer a single headline that ties cost to predictability, not raw speed. e.g., \"Predictable latency, predictable costs\". keep hero copy tight.

priya: for visuals I like a scatter with iso-cost contours for the latency vs cost chart. second chart should be a mini funnel showing how batching/caching reduces unit cost for common seq lengths. i'll mock comps by noon.

sam: data note — our benchmark set uses 8 workloads (chat, search, summarization, code). i'll export median + 95th percentile latencies and cost per 1k tokens. will add a small table for SI.

lina: webinar: 20–30m + 10m q&a. section ideas: 1) market problem (unpredictable token ops), 2) demo: same prompt across 3 routing policies (fast, balanced, cheap), 3) deep dive into charts and config knobs, 4) customer stories + CTA to book Dedicated trial.

maya: routing rules (inbound): we want two CTAs — \"Try now (hosted)\" and \"Book a dedicated consult\". leads with >50k monthly tokens should auto-flag for AE follow-up. smaller leads go into self-serve nurture. can ops add source tags? @jon

jon: yep — tagging plan: utm_campaign=bench_launch, utm_source=webinar/landing, lead_size=estimated_tokens. set `lead_size` buckets: <50k, 50k-500k, >500k. AE pings for >50k.

priya: microcopy proposals for hero: \"Speed you can predict. Costs you can control.\" alternatives: \"Latency that scales, economics that make sense.\" which lands better?

lina: i vote the first (predict/control) — clearer benefit.

sam: quick chart specs so eng can reproduce:
```
chart1: scatter(latency_median_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens)
  color=model_variant, size=throughput
  overlay: cost_iso_lines([0.01,0.05,0.1])
  annotate: typical chat seq=64 tokens

chart2: waterfall unit-cost reduction
  baseline: no batching/no-cache
  steps: batching(8), kv_cache(prefix=common), quantized_model_variant
  y-axis: $/1k tokens
```

maya: love it. Priya — keep colors brand-friendly and accessible. Sam — can you commit the CSV by 4pm so Priya can mock?

sam: yes, pushing CSV to /shared/bench/launch/ by 3:45pm. will include the scripts used (repro note).

priya: mock ETA 6pm PST. will post 2 variants: conservative and exaggerated for A/B testing.

lina: webinar promo copy: short intro (40–60 chars) + 1-line description + CTA. draft: \"Make LLM inference predictable: latency, cost, and the knobs that matter. Join our benchmark walk-through.\" Thoughts?

jon: good. for landing page we need 3 quick lead magnets: 1) benchmark PDF, 2) short 5-min demo video, 3) ROI calculator microtool. put the PDF behind email capture, video freely available.

maya: inbound flow: webinar signup -> email drip (3 messages) -> if lead_size >50k then manual AE reach + calendar invite. If >500k also trigger solutions-eng alert. otherwise send nurture series and product tour.

priya: visual ask for landing: hero chart variant (small), short bullets, CTA. below fold: full-size interactive scatter. we can add toggle for model variant and seq length.

maya: okay decisions recap:
- hero copy: \"Speed you can predict. Costs you can control.\"
- charts: scatter w/ iso-lines + unit-cost waterfall
- webinar: 25m + QA, outline as above
- inbound routing: lead_size buckets, >50k AE ping, >500k SE alert
- assets: benchmark PDF, demo vid, ROI tool

lina: can we set an internal pre-launch review Fri 9am? want marketing + eng + product to sign off on metrics and slide deck.

jon: scheduled. calendar invite from me.

maya: final ask — short bullets for PR/social: 1) what we measured, 2) key takeaway (predictable latency => lower unit cost with routing), 3) link to benchmark PDF. i'll draft and iterate.

deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled mock deploy of landing page will run at 2026-03-27T02:00:00Z.

sam: noted, i'll run a quick smoke on the metrics export then.

maya: thanks everyone — i'll compile action items and update the doc. cc @jon @priya @sam @lina :thumbsup:

jon: :rocket:

priya: :art:

lina: :calendar:
